definition: A decoding strategy that restricts sampling to the k most probable next tokens at each step, discarding the rest of the distribution.
details: Top-k sampling balances diversity and quality by preventing the model from sampling extremely unlikely (and often nonsensical) tokens while still allowing some randomness.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Top-k Sampling.
